m2-coverage-script.title: Write scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py
m2-coverage-script.imperative: Write a standalone stdlib-only CLI script scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py, matching the style of scripts/verify_state_note.py / scripts/verify_cycles.py: holds an explicit, commented list of (template_path, gate_id) worktree-entering pairs (today exactly one: skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json, gate init), with a module docstring explaining why this is a maintained list, not an auto-detector. Missing -> exit 1, name the offending template + gate. All wired -> exit 0, print the count of templates checked. CLI: python scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py [--root PATH].

m3-tests.title: Land tests/test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py with both deliberate-breakage tests
m3-tests.imperative: Write tests/test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py (test-after allowed per handoff Test Mode, but the deliberate-breakage tests themselves ARE the acceptance criteria). Enumeration deliberate breakage: copy COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json into a tmp_path fixture, strip the new precondition from the copy's init gate, run the coverage script against that broken copy and assert exit code 1/nonzero; then run it against the real fixed repo tree and assert exit 0 -- both assertions in the same test. Engine deliberate breakage: using scripts/checklist_engine.py's Python API (pattern from tests/test_checklist_engine.py), build a minimal in-memory/tmp_path gated checklist with one init-like gate carrying the new precondition, call start() with a --here path that does NOT match the real git rev-parse --show-toplevel and assert EngineError naming the unmet precondition; then fix the expected path and assert start() succeeds. Both deliberate-breakage constructions run in tmp_path/temp fixtures only, never against this worktree's own .git or the shared checkout, and clean up automatically as pytest teardown. TDD red is not required per test-after mode; go straight to the passing test file plus the manual proof that a reverted fix flips a specific assertion from green to red (documented at m4).
